title: Finite stabilized construction for supported perfect maps
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], U a quasi-compact open, and T a closed subset with quasi-compact complement. Let E belong to D_QCoh(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. Let S_n be a sequence in D(O_U), with isomorphisms h_n: S_(n+1) ≅ S_n ⊕ S_n[1]. Assume S_0 is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] and supported on T intersect U. Let a_n: S_n → E|U satisfy a_(n+1) = a_n composed with the first projection composed with h_n. Then there exist n, a perfect R on X supported on T, beta: R → E, and e: R|U ≅ S_n such that beta|U = a_n composed with e. No retraction is part of this conclusion.

proof.text: Choose finitely many affine opens whose union with U is X. Attach them successively, maintaining a global-on-the-current-union perfect supported source and a map to the restricted E. Initially these are S(0) and a(0). The intersections and the complements of T in the affines are quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness.

At one attachment V, apply affine supported extension to the current source on the overlap. Its extension Q is supported on T intersect V and restricts to the overlap source plus its shift. Compose the overlap isomorphism, the first projection, and the current map to E.
Use affine perfect map lifting on V to replace Q by a perfect tensor augmentation, invertible on the overlap, retaining support on T intersect V and lifting this map to E restricted to V.

Glue this map on V with the first-projection map on the old union using derived open gluing. The affine lifting equation gives compatibility. Perfectness and support of the glued source are local; canonical iterated restriction comparisons identify its restriction on U with S(k+1), and ha identifies the restricted map with a(k+1). Repeat over the finite cover. The resulting n, R, beta and isomorphism satisfy the construction equation; no summand maps are asserted or used.
